newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS, SELES TO MEET IN FINAL AT HILTON HEAD ISLAND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS, SELES TO MEET IN FINAL AT HILTON HEAD ISLAND.

text.p: Martina Hingis, the new number one player in the world, stumbled slightly on Saturday before beating Brenda Schultz-Mccarthy to advance to the final of the $926,250 Family Circle Cup against Monica Seles.
Hingis, the tournament's top seed, dropped the first set, her first loss of a set in the tournament, but the 16-year-old Swiss came back to win 5-7 6-3 6-2 and remain undefeated in 1997 at 30-0.
The final will be a rematch of last week's Lipton Championships, won by Hingis 6-2 6-1. Seles, the third seed, defeated two-time champion Conchita Martinez of Spain, the fifth seed, 6-3 6-4.

Hingis had to overcome a powerful serve from the 14th-seeded Schultz-McCarthy, who cranked serves as fast as 117 mph (187 kph) in the first set and was consistently over 100 mph (160 kph) on first serves throughout the match.

Schultz-McCarthy broke Hingis in the third game of the first set, then held to go up 3-1. Hingis then held and broke the Dutchwoman in the sixth game to make it 3-3, taking advantage of Schultz-McCarthy's inability to get in any first serves.

The players then held serve until Schultz-McCarthy broke Hingis by fighting off a game point to go up 6-5. The Dutch player then took the set 7-5 with a more consistent serve, including a 112 mph (179 kph) ace.
But Hingis did a better job returning serve and Schultz-McCarthy began making more errors in the next two sets.
"I was a little upset that I lost the first set and then I tried to be more aggressive and just didn't rush any more," Hingis said. "I just tried to hit balls in the court and make her move."
Hingis quickly got up 3-0 in the second set. Each player held serve the rest of the set to even the match at a set apiece.
Hingis broke a tiring Schultz-McCarthy twice in the third set to go up 3-0 again and eventually won the set 6-3 on serve.
Hingis said she had a simple strategy against Schultz-McCarthy's strong serve.
"Just try to hit it back, joked the young Swiss, now 3-0 lifetime against Schultz-McCarthy. "I know that I have a pretty good return. It's one of the strengths of my game."
Schultz-McCarthy, who knocked off third seet Jana Novotna and sixth seed Linda Davenport to get to the semifinals, said Friday's three-set win over Davenport took a lot out of her.
"I think I got tired," she said. "I have to admit, it was a tough match (Friday) and I had to dig deep to get to this match."
Her fatigue may have played a part in her 53 unforced errors in the match.
Despite suffering from effects of a virus that left her unable to speak above a whisper at a post-match news conference, Seles had a far easier time on the court than Hingis.
She needed only an hour and five minutes to advance to the final in straight sets against Martinez, a clay-court specialist who won this event in 1994 and 1995.

"I wanted to come out very aggressive today against her, try to take control of the point," said Seles, who was unable to practice before the match because of her ill health. "I was pretty successful and on a couple key points I just went for them and they went in today."
Seles looked sharp, using her powerful two-handed forehands and backhands to keep Martinez off-balance.

"She put a lot of pressure on me, hitting the balls very hard," said Martinez. "I couldn't keep the ball deep and high. You play short against Monica and she's going to win the points. I don't think I played my best."
Seles said she is looking forward to playing Hingis, who replaced Steffi Graf atop the world rankings Monday.
"It's really exciting," Seles said. "The tennis Martina has been playing this year is unbelievable. It's a tough job ahead of me. I'll just go out there and do the best that I can."
